review: 1:1–1:2 and 4:7–4:8 repeat the same address ('Jesus, You are my Lord / my dear, faithful One'); the Arabic frames the hymn with it, so Hebrew repeats it word for word.
1:5–1:6 אֶתְיַגֵּעַ / בְּדַרְכִּי הֵנָּה — 'why do I toil on my way here'; the Arabic تُرَى لِمَاذَا is a rhetorical 'why, then', which Hebrew marks with מַדּוּעַ alone.
2:2 אַתָּה עִמָּדִי — 'You are with me' (Ps 23:4); the Arabic مُلَازِمِي ('clinging to me') is stronger, but the psalm echo is what the tune wants.
3:1 לֹא־הִטְעָה אוֹתִי — 'it did not deceive me'; the Arabic passive مَخْدُوع ('I was not deceived') becomes active in Hebrew, which has no natural passive of this verb here.
3:6 מוֹשָׁב חָמוּד — 'a desirable dwelling'; the Arabic الْمَسْكِنَ الْمَرْغُوب is a participle phrase, and the Hebrew adjective keeps the line at six.
